# Reactions and braking observations

`reactions.tsv` records four actual private Java methods on distinct, real placed organisms.
Source twice and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
All four compiled helper classes match across both backends.
The fixture contains 186 cases, 654 snapshots, 1,962 actor views, and 468 explicit calls.
Every actor view contains the complete 154-field organism observation schema.

## Comparison contract

The fixed ledger precedes Rust replay.
Compare scalar, velocity, effect, gas, statistics, endpoint, bound, ARGB, reaction, identity, order, and RNG observations exactly.
Only `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the existing organism geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Check geometric NaN classification and signed infinity explicitly.
Do not apply this allowance to velocities or other scalar state.

Only `_world` and `_visibleWorld` are named organism collaborator exclusions.
Setup selection remains source callback-routing metadata.
All other recorded observations remain comparison obligations.
Whole-genome reference identity connects actor, infected, saved, and statistics holders.
Full G/N blocks record every genome and gene value.
The separate genetics fixture covers per-Gene mutable-object alias topology.

## Actual execution and inputs

Compile `tools/reference/ReactionOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.ReactionOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the isolated arguments recorded in provenance.
The helper validates four explicit profile roots through `toRealPath` before accessing the simulation.
It rejects existing output directories and uses `CREATE_NEW` for the fixture.
Six negative invocations cover every omitted root, an escaped profile symlink, and existing output preservation.
Positive processes have a 120-second bound; negative processes have a 30-second bound.
The existing runner cleans each owned process group.

Each case resets actual source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive settings.
Initial organism attempts are zero; initial oxygen is `1000`.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`; meta mutation is zero.
GREEN selection weight is seven; other selectable weights are zero.
The setup seed is `827364`.
Most cases supply TEAL cost `0.25` and velocity/rotation limits `1000000`.
Payment cases supply TEAL cost `1`.
Individual settings record every cost, rubbing coefficient, and hidden limit used.

The helper creates real `VisibleWorld(null)` and World objects.
It invokes actual gas-add, organism construction, paste, and World.addOrganism methods.
Peer, victim, and killer are added in that order, at `(1000,1000)`, `(3500,3500)`, and `(2000,2000)`.
Their initial numeric IDs are `0`, `1`, and `2`.
Peer is selected before the first add, avoiding MainWindow callbacks without mocks.
The actual reaction peer is always the distinct killer organism.
No self-contact or fake collaborator is supplied.

Five initial genotype identities are recorded before actor construction.
Victim uses explicit `g0`; killer and peer use explicit one-GREEN-gene `g1` and `g2`.
`g3` and `g4` use actual GeneticCode.clone on `g0`.
Victim initially holds `g3` as infection and `g4` as saved code.
Ordinary victim genes are TEAL and GREEN, with length `12` and theta `index * 0.25`.
The first branch is zero; subsequent branches are `-1`.
All gene reactions begin zero; controlled phenotype reaction arrays remain separate inputs.
Symmetry is one, mirror is zero, and constructor booleans are false.
Spore modifier is one; generation is `41`; clade is `root`.
Other supplied gene counts, colors, and lengths remain explicit input G/N records.
Later snapshots never supply construction inputs.

Setup controls give victim and killer energy `1000`.
Victim can-dodge starts false.
Killer plant, consumer, fungus, auburn, enhanced, plague, spore, and kill classifications start cleared.
Labelled cases then supply their explicit classification changes.
Cached endpoint arrays contain distinct supplied integer vectors with valid segment counts.
These controls observe source method arithmetic; they do not assert physical contact eligibility.
Actual construction mass, inertia, body arrays, bounds, flags, and caches remain observed.

Each action resets actual Random through a recorded `rng:seed` control.
Ordinary actions use seed zero and velocities `0.75`, `-0.5`, and `0.03125`.
Gate cases supply their labelled seeds instead.
The bounded threshold search uses actual `Random.nextInt(10)` and records its selected input seed.
It does not supply scripted Random outputs.
`R` peeks through a serialized Random copy without consuming the actual stream.

Palette and precedence cases supply two base-six reaction input vectors.
The vectors vary all 36 channels without calculating biological expectations.
Their third call observes braking with every reaction set to one.
Individual-channel cases instead supply one nonzero channel.
All results come from original method calls and direct observations.

Both reaction methods scan actuators in reverse order and stop after the first eligible segment.
The selected reaction belongs to the supplied contact segment, not the actuator.
Mode three reads segment zero's start coordinates.
Endpoint and center differences use wrapping Java integer subtraction before double arithmetic.
Friendly acceleration and moving/nonmoving brakes retain their separate coefficients.
Random gates precede energy payment; rotation draws follow successful payment.
Partial payment remains consumed when the source reports failure.
Reactions and brakes retain their different injured-self dispatch.

## Initial setup correction

The first unpublished run supplied double values for integer center controls and failed before writing a fixture.
Its helper, compiled classes, and failed receipt remain preserved.
Source declares `_centerX` and `_centerY` as integers at `Organism.java:375` and `Organism.java:379`.
Separate `_dCenterX` and `_dCenterY` fields store double centers.
The corrected input cases use actual integer centers, including both overflow directions.
No expected output or tolerance changed.
The provenance records the separate Rust mode-five correction and failing regression evidence.

## Schema and ledger

Rows use the existing `C/U/I/A/P/K/O/H/W/S/T/G/N/R/E` schema.
Doubles use sixteen hexadecimal raw IEEE digits.
Arrays preserve comma-separated order; null references use `~`.
`K` contains stage, original method name, victim role, and `killer,segment,peer_segment`.
Reflection invokes the actual private method with those arguments.
`I rng:seed` has type `long`; integer center controls have type `int`.
Cached endpoint controls use `int[]`; reaction controls retain all 36 independent `int[]` fields.

Each snapshot includes H references, ten World values, 52 statistics fields, 49 getters, full G/N, and RNG suffix.
No V/Q/J tree or corridor observations occur in this fixture.
The provenance records actual commands, exits, hashes, equality, guards, and 74 reference preservation checks.
All 25 preexisting TSVs retain their pinned hashes.

This fixture does not execute physical contact detection, contact eligibility, full frames, UI, or networking.
It does not establish save migration or distributable acceptance.
Explicit raw scalar and cache controls do not claim player UI acceptance.
Java observation provenance does not claim Rust replay results.
